title: DNS over QUIC RFC 9250 Foundation Architecture
purpose: Define the first DNS over QUIC adapter boundary above the managed QUIC transport, covering ALPN, default port policy, DoQ error-code constants, and DNS message length-prefix framing.
design_summary: The DoQ foundation is implemented as a new `Incursa.Quic.Dns` adapter package above the core transport. `DoqDefaults` owns the ALPN token `doq`, default endpoint helpers for UDP port 853, and validation that rejects UDP port 53. `DoqErrorCode` owns the RFC 9250 application error-code values. `DoqMessageCodec` owns the two-octet big-endian DNS message length prefix and leaves DNS payload semantics to a later DNS parser or resolver boundary.
data_and_state_considerations: The foundation slice is stateless. It validates option bags before connection or listener startup and encodes or decodes one framed DNS payload at a time. The codec supports span-based encoding and decoding so later stream readers can reuse it without forcing transport-core allocations or DNS parser coupling.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The DoQ adapter may add ALPN `doq` when the caller has not supplied any ALPN protocols, but it rejects an explicit non-DoQ ALPN list.
UDP port 53 is rejected for client and listener endpoint helpers because RFC 9250 reserves DoQ for port 853 or an explicitly agreed alternate port.
A partial length prefix or a partial payload is reported as incomplete by `TryDecode` and as a DoQ protocol error by `Decode`.
Payloads larger than 65535 bytes cannot be encoded in the RFC 9250 two-octet length prefix.
risks: This foundation slice does not yet prove end-to-end query/response stream mapping; that remains a later stream-adapter slice.
Padding policy, connection reuse, cancellation/reset handling, 0-RTT, Retry/address validation, and zone-transfer concurrency remain separate RFC 9250 slices.
Putting DNS resolver semantics in `Incursa.Quic` would blur the transport boundary; the adapter package keeps that behavior out of `QuicConnectionRuntime`.

supplemental_sections.heading: Implementation Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: The QUIC transport remains responsible for TLS, streams, flow control, and packet processing. The DoQ package owns application protocol constants and DNS-message framing above those streams. Full request/response dispatch will build on this adapter surface in a later slice.
